title: Polynomial-Time Branching on Zero
statement: Let $f$ map Boolean words to natural numbers, and let $a,b$ map Boolean words to Boolean words. If the unary encoding of $f$ and the word functions $a,b$ are polynomial-time computable, then the function that returns $a(z)$ when $f(z)=0$ and $b(z)$ otherwise is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: The unary word function $z\mapsto 1^{f(z)}$ is polynomial-time computable
The word function $a$ is polynomial-time computable
The word function $b$ is polynomial-time computable
replaced: If a unary value and two word functions are polynomial-time computable, then so is the function returning the first word when the value is zero and the second otherwise.
